original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.

Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Decide whether one six-source characteristic-6 floor word can keep the multiset (6,6,6,7,7,7) at every diagonal index s=4..18. Classify the splits of that multiset at s=4 and at s=18, and exhibit a monotone chain for every constant-mask pair, together with one chain whose mask moves.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for one new connector operation. This package keeps the unsigned dirty connector alphabet fixed and answers the first open question of PR7029: whether splits of the type-T1 multiset (6,6,6,7,7,7) at s=4 and s=18 can sit in one monotone chain. A new operation is not the missing step.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the recursive-interface schedule. It does not change a supplier, a consumer, or kappa. The witness shows that the diagonal chain for this multiset is nonempty, which is the case PR7029 left after proving that the (0, 9) hypothesis is what excludes it.
stop_rule: Stop once the endpoint splits are classified, every constant-mask pair is realized by an explicit pure-slide word, and one mask-changing word is checked. Do not search the unequal-mask graph, do not classify pairs with s+t=15, and do not rerun the separation-3 or centre censuses.
evidence: Exhaustive finite census of the endpoint domains: 20 splits at s=18, all with q_18 identically 3 and a weight-3 bridge, and 756 pairs (q_4, w_35) of which 60 are type A and 60 are type B. Explicit construction of 120 pure-slide floor words, one for every constant mask and every final letter, each keeping the vector 7 on that mask at every s=4..18. One further floor word moves the mask from {0,1,2} at s=4 to {0,1,4} at s=5..18. Ten controls. No SAT solver was run. The unrestricted depth-two exclusion is not claimed.

open_questions.question: Which endpoint pairs with unequal masks are joined by a monotone chain of the multiset (6,6,6,7,7,7)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every equal-mask pair is realized by a pure-slide word, and one unequal pair is realized by an explicit word, so existence of some chain is settled. The remaining question is the boundary of mask transport inside this multiset. A missing pair would be an obstruction that uses neither the (0, 9) hypothesis nor a frozen 12. A complete yes would mean this multiset imposes no further diagonal obstruction beyond the two endpoint lemmas. Either answer stays short of the unrestricted c=6 exclusion.
open_questions.first_step: Search the finite (r, f) graph for one symmetry class, M_4={0,1,2}, D=3, M_18={3,4,5}, where r is the number of early letters still to place and f is the number of late letters still to place.
open_questions.blocked_by: The constant-mask proof uses equal early and late budgets on each source, and those budgets differ as soon as the masks differ. This package does not search that graph.
